newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank meets, with no policy changes expected.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank meets, with no policy changes expected.

text.p: The Bundesbank's policy-making council met on Thursday with economists agreed that a cut in the bank's leading interest rates was extremely unlikely.
In a Reuter poll conducted this week, all 10 economists polled said they expected the discount and Lombard rates to remain unchanged at 2.50 percent and 4.50 percent respectively.
The bank's main money market rate, the securities repurchase rate or repo, is seen holding steady at three percent, the rate which has prevailed since August.

Economists said that although recent signs about the economy have not been strong, gross domestic product should start to pick up, leaving the Bundesbank little reason to provide a stimulus with lower interest rates.
About the only chance for excitement on Thursday could come in a special announcement that the Bundesbank would free repo business from minimum reserve requirements.
But according to the economists, the odds of that happening are slim with only one of the 10 expecting the central bank to make such a move.
Several, however, said they thought the Bundesbank was moving towards abolishing the reserve requirement on repos and could decide to do so before the end of the year.
In Germany, banks must deposit a certain percentage of short-term borrowings from foreign banks and domestic non-banks in non-interest bearing deposits at the Bundesbank.
The minimum reserve requirement is widely seen as a burden which has prompted banks to shift their repurchase business in German securities from Frankfurt to London.
Currently, the level on repo business and sight deposits is two percent, and 1.5 percent on savings deposits.

Under a repo transaction, a dealer borrows funds from an investor by selling securities to him. The dealer repurchases the securities at a later date, thereby repaying the loan. The difference between the sale and repurchase price represents interest on the loan.
